First, let's factor the expression as a perfect square trinomial in ${b}^{2}.$ We have

$$
\begin{aligned}16{x}^{4}+8{x}^{2}+1 & ={(4{x}^{2})}^{2}+2\cdot (4{x}^{2})\cdot 1+{1}^{2} \\  & ={(4{x}^{2}+1)}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we need to factor the sum of squares in the parentheses. To do this, we first write it as a difference. Then, we rewrite the second term using ${i}^{2}=-1.$ Finally, we factor as a difference of squares.

$$
\begin{aligned}4{x}^{2}+1 & =4{x}^{2}-(-1) \\  & =4{x}^{2}-({i}^{2}) \\  & ={(2x)}^{2}-{(i)}^{2} \\  & =(2x+i)(2x-i)\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, substituting this back into our main expression, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}16{x}^{4}+8{x}^{2}+1 & ={(4{x}^{2}+1)}^{2} \\  & ={((2x+i)(2x-i))}^{2} \\  & ={(2x+i)}^{2}{(2x-i)}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
